spec.title: `flow:managed-blocks` — write into files you do not own

p.PACKAGE-INSTALLS-THE-MANAGED-BLOCKS-DISC: A `flow` package that installs one discipline: **how a tool writes into a file it does not own** — an agent-instruction file, a shell rc, an ssh config, a shared project config — without destroying what the other tenants put there.

p.AUDIENCE-IS-TOOL-AUTHORS: **Audience: tool authors.** Anyone whose software writes into files it does not solely own.

p.IF-YOUR-TOOL-WRITES-A-FILE-OTHERS-EDIT-T: If your tool `write()`s a file a human or another tool also edits, this is for you.

p.the-law-fits-on-one-line: The law fits on one line:

spec.fence: Own exactly one delimited block; never touch a byte outside it.

p.package-contents-lead: This package ships three pieces of content plus a boot snippet:

facts.CONTENT-THE-PROTOCOL: `spec/flows/managed-blocks/MANAGED-BLOCKS-PROTOCOL.xml` — the full protocol: the co-tenant law, marker design (unique, greppable, paired, self-documenting, versioned), the absent / present / malformed state machine, the three verbs (create / update / remove), plan-time classification, the byte-identical no-op, and multi-tool cohabitation.
facts.CONTENT-THE-REJECTED-DESIGNS: `spec/flows/managed-blocks/rejected-designs.xml` — four designs that look reasonable and are wrong (sidecar, model-based detection, auto-repair, whole-file ownership), each with its full why, plus the malformed-state hard-stop drill.
facts.CONTENT-THE-ADOPTION-GUIDE: `spec/flows/managed-blocks/adoption-guide.xml` — migrating an overwriting tool onto a block, a fixture table that pins the state machine, and what belongs inside the block versus a tool-owned file it points at.
facts.CONTENT-THE-BOOT-SNIPPET: `spec/boot/65-flow-managed-blocks.xml` — boot snippet loaded at session start: the one-line law, when to read the protocol, and the never-do list.

p.UNINSTALL-REMOVES-EVERY-FILE-THE-PACKAGE: Uninstalling removes every file the package wrote, including the boot snippet.

p.USER-OWNED-FILES-ARE-NEVER-TOUCHED: User-owned files are never touched — which is, fittingly, the whole point of the practice.

facts.COMPOSES-ATTRIBUTION-POLICY-AND-WAL: `flow:git-attribution-policy` and `flow:wal` — their instruction files are exactly the kind of shared, hand-authored file this protocol protects. A tool that writes an attribution snippet or a WAL redirect into `CLAUDE.md` must do it as a block, not an overwrite.
facts.COMPOSES-CONFLICT-PROTOCOL: `flow:conflict-protocol` — a malformed block is a conflict surfaced to the human, never silently resolved; both practices refuse to guess when two writers disagree, and both hard-stop instead of auto-fixing.

p.practice-crystallized-from-the-origin-pr: The practice is crystallized from the origin project's managed-redirect-block law — the rule that a tool owns one delimited, machine-findable region of a shared file and never touches a byte outside it, with a hard stop on any malformed state.

p.ORIGIN-MARKERS-ARE-ONE-EXAMPLE-AND-THE-R: The origin's own markers (`<vibevm>`) and host file (`CLAUDE.md`) appear here only as one worked example among others (shell rc, ssh config); the rule is generic to any tool and any shared file.

p.collections-spirit-is-the-redbook: The collection's spirit is the book *AI-native development*, which ships in Russian inside `flow:redbook` at `spec/book/ru/`.
